Cluster 4 · PGR Precision & Berry Quality

GA3 & CPPU Protocol + Pink Berry, Cracking, Shatter & Shot Berries

Direct Answer · EU-Safe GA3 & CPPU Protocol

For export-grade Thompson Seedless, spray GA3 10 ppm pre-bloom (pH 5.5–6.0), 15–20 ppm at 50% & 90% capfall, and dip at 3–4 mm & 6–7 mm in GA3 30–40 ppm OR GA3 25–30 ppm + CPPU 1–2 ppm strictly once. Exceeding 2 ppm CPPU triggers thick skin, <16°Brix, shatter, and EU MRL rejection [ICAR-NRCG].

Step-by-Step EU-Safe GA3, 6-BA & CPPU Schedule (ICAR-NRCG)

Direct Answer · PGR Stage Doses & MRL Traps

Never substitute repeated CCC (Chlormequat Chloride / Lihocin) sprays for April sub-cane pinching (5–7 leaves), and never exceed 2 ppm CPPU in berry dips. Always acidify GA3 spray water to pH 5.5–6.0 for uniform panicle elongation and berry sizing [ICAR-NRCG; APEDA 2026].

Physiological Disorders: Pink Berry, Cracking, Shatter, Shot & Water Berry

Direct Answer · Preventing Grape Physiological Disorders

Pink Berry stems from cold-night/warm-day swings on sun-exposed clusters (fix: diffused Y-trellis shade + bunch bags). Berry Cracking & Shatter come from irregular veraison drip, Ca shortage, late N, >22°Brix over-ripening, or >2 ppm CPPU. Shot Berries respond to pre-bloom 0.1% B + 0.25% Zn [ICAR-NRCG; APEDA].

Small / Scarred Berry Triage
PREVENTABLE · PRE-BLOOM B+Zn

Shot Berries (Boron / Zinc / Cold)

Micronutrient Deficiency or Late Nov Prune
  • Many tiny pea-sized green berries remain mixed beside normal berries
  • Smooth skin (no corky rings) — caused by poor pollination/fertilization
  • Worse when Oct pruning slips into late Nov cold or B/Zn is deficient
Field Fix: Spray 0.1% Boron + 0.25% Zinc pre-bloom (verify water B <1 ppm!). Keep Oct pruning in optimal window and confirm 45 DAP petiole B & Zn at 30–50 ppm [ICAR-NRCG].
CURABLE · EARLY IPM (<8 mm)

Thrips Scab / Russet Ring

Scirtothrips dorsalis / Rhipiphorothrips
  • Corky brown halo/scab ring around berry stem end or sides
  • Silvery curled young leaf tips at pre-bloom to 8 mm stage
  • Rejects EU export lots visually even when Brix is >=16°
Field Fix: Install 25 blue sticky traps/ha at sprout; when >5 thrips/shoot, rotate Spinosad (0.25–0.3 ml/L) or Emamectin benzoate (0.22–0.4 g/L) strictly within NRCG Annexure-5 PHI [ICAR-NRCG].
Veraison & Post-Harvest Berry Triage
CANOPY FIX · NOT FUNGAL

Pink Berry Syndrome

Abiotic Sun + Cold-Night / Warm-Day Swing
  • Unwanted pink/blush pigmentation on white Thompson Seedless clusters
  • Concentrated on sun-exposed outer bunches during Jan–Feb temperature swings
  • Berries stay intact on pedicel but lose uniform green-amber export grade
Field Fix: Maintain diffused Y-trellis leaf canopy shade, skirt/paper-bag exposed bunches, and maintain balanced K/Ca nutrition without excess late N [ICAR-NRCG].
IRREVERSIBLE + EU MRL RISK

CPPU Overdose Shatter & Cracking

CPPU >2 ppm / Late N / Irregular Drip
  • Abnormally thick crunchy berry skin, delayed sugar (<16°Brix), loose pedicels
  • Berries split vertically after uneven veraison watering or drop inside export box
  • CPPU >2 ppm triggers EU MRL failure and post-harvest shatter
Field Fix: NEVER exceed 1–2 ppm CPPU (strictly once). Keep veraison drip steady (8–12 L/vine/day), supply early Tank-B Calcium, pre-cool 4–6 hrs to 0–1°C, and pack with dual-release SO2 pads [APEDA].

GA3, CPPU & Berry Disorder FAQs

What is the EU-safe GA3 and CPPU berry sizing protocol for Thompson Seedless?

Spray GA3 10 ppm pre-bloom (2–3 in panicle, water pH 5.5–6.0), GA3 15–20 ppm at 50% and 90% capfall, and dip at 3–4 mm and 6–7 mm in GA3 30–40 ppm OR GA3 25–30 ppm + CPPU 1–2 ppm strictly once [ICAR-NRCG].

Why should growers never exceed 2 ppm CPPU or repeat CCC (Lihocin) sprays?

CPPU above 2 ppm produces crunchy thick skin, delays sugar below 16°Brix, triggers post-harvest berry shatter, and causes EU MRL failure. Repeated Chlormequat Chloride (CCC) sprays are a top EU rejection trigger — use mechanical sub-cane pinching (5–7 leaves) instead [ICAR-NRCG; APEDA].

How do you prevent Pink Berry Syndrome, berry cracking, and shot berries?

Prevent Pink Berry with diffused Y-trellis shade, bunch skirting/bags, and balanced K/Ca. Prevent cracking with steady veraison drip (8–12 L/vine/day) and early Tank-B Calcium. Prevent shot berries with pre-bloom 0.1% B + 0.25% Zn (verifying water B < 1 ppm) [ICAR-NRCG].
